o1.said: Simulated in Python by NVIDIA Warp. Drawn by three p p. And the data never leaves the GPU.

k1.said: Warp turns a Python function into a GPU kernel: one thread for every particle, all running at once.

m1.said: No trip to the C P U and back: Warp writes the cloth and the sparks straight into buffers it shares with the renderer.

m2.said: So the ray tracer sees every fold in the same frame.

n1.said: With no copies in the way, it scales. This blast is millions of particles.

f1.said: And back the other way: the finished frame goes straight to a Warp kernel, which turns it into an event camera.

e1.said: Cloth, sparks, jelly, water, fire. Python on the GPU, drawn by three p p.
